decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach to the key on the right; keep left parked. Key appears farther inward than reference.
Continue smooth elbow-up arc, pitching right gripper toward a downward approach while tracking the key.
Bring right wrist inward above the key while completing downward pitch; use smooth moderate increments.
Center the right open gripper over the key and finish a near-vertical pinch orientation, matching its slight table yaw.
Use wrist view to move the open pinch inward onto the shaft near the bow and refine yaw before closing.
Refine wrist-image centering at the neck of the key and correct yaw in the opposite direction; keep open until aligned.
Straighten the key shaft in the wrist view and bring the bow-neck junction between the right fingers.
Key neck is now centered and nearly straight. Settle slightly lower and close the right gripper around the shaft.
Allow the right fingers to finish closing, then begin a small test lift; retention will be judged from the key image.
Lift the right-held key clear of the table with the gripper kept closed, checking that it remains fixed between the fingers.
Key is retained in the wrist view. Raise and yaw the right hand toward an inward-facing handover while remaining on its own side.
Continue right-hand yaw and elevation while starting a smooth elbow-up receiving approach with the left arm.
Advance left receiving wrist on a continuous elbow-up arc; finish positioning the retained key near the central handover space.
Bring the left hand forward in its own workspace and finish right yaw for presentation of the key bow. Maintain separated wrists.
Continue shaping the left hand into a side-on receiving pose while the right hand holds the key steady.
Finish left side-on alignment outside the key bow, then narrow its opening in preparation for the handover.
Advance the left receiving fingers toward the exposed bow, keeping right grip closed until the receiving pinch is established.
Complete the short receiving approach and close the left fingers on the key bow while maintaining the right hold.
Settle the receiving pinch, then open the right gripper without moving either wrist to transfer the key to the left.
Withdraw the opened right hand outward while keeping the left pinch fixed; inspect retention after separation.
Key is visibly retained by the left hand. Begin raising and rotating it upright over the lock while clearing the right arm outward.
Replan from the interrupted pose using half-sized left rotation/translation increments to preserve elbow-up joint continuity.
Rotate the left-held key progressively toward vertical while raising clearance and keeping the right hand parked clear.
Continue the left wrist’s smooth upright rotation and elevated approach; key remains visible in the receiving pinch.
Raise the retained key and continue rotating toward an upright insertion pose above the left-side lock.
Continue the elevated upright rotation with modest increments, preserving the left grasp and elbow-up continuity.
Bring the left-held key closer to vertical above the lock, maintaining clearance for visual alignment.
Finish the upright orientation above the lock; next use the close wrist view to refine slot centering and yaw.
The slot is yawed relative to the upright key. Rotate the left wrist above the surface to align the blade with the visible slot before descent.
Refine remaining slot yaw and shift a few millimeters toward its center, with a slow initial descent while the key remains upright.
Fine-center the blade laterally over the now nearly parallel slot and lower another small amount for close insertion alignment.
The blade and slot are visually centered and parallel. Lower vertically in small increments, maintaining the left grip and upright alignment.
Continue the aligned vertical insertion slowly, keeping the key upright and the left gripper closed; watch for displacement at contact.
The key shifted relative to the fingers during descent, suggesting edge contact. Relieve insertion pressure with a short vertical retreat before refining alignment.
Retreat farther from the slot and correct a small in-plane offset; the key’s changed appearance makes retention and insertion depth uncertain.
The key is again stable relative to the left fingers after retreat. Test a slow vertical insertion at the corrected planar alignment.
Continue cautiously downward with the stable key centered at the slot, checking for any renewed slipping or edge contact.
Lower a final short increment while maintaining the corrected alignment and closed left grip; assess seating before attempting the turn.
At the seated height, attempt a small controlled turn without further downward motion; monitor whether the key remains coupled to the left grip.
Continue the controlled turn at fixed insertion height, with the left grip closed and no added downward pressure.
Advance the turn smoothly while maintaining the seated height and closed left grip; the key remains centered in the wrist view.
Complete the last small portion of the turn at fixed height, then reassess the key and slot rather than assuming completion from tracking.
Check final seating with only a five-millimeter descent while retaining the turned pose; insertion depth remains visually uncertain.
The key has shifted within the pinch during seating. Relieve contact and bring it back toward slot alignment before attempting a more secure seating.
Return closer to insertion yaw without downward motion, keeping the shifted key retained for a controlled regrasp if needed.
Lift clear of the lock while restoring insertion yaw so the displaced key can be inspected without additional contact.
Refine the remaining fore-aft slot offset visible after retreat, with only a shallow descent and the left pinch retained.
With the blade tip now centered on the slot mouth, advance vertically by a small amount and watch for renewed slipping.
Correct the small lateral offset at the mouth and advance another shallow increment while retaining the stable key.
At the refined seated alignment, begin the turn again without further descent, retaining the key in the left fingers.
Continue the seated turn smoothly, keeping translation fixed and monitoring the key’s stable position between the left fingers.
Complete approximately a quarter-turn-scale motion from insertion alignment and settle without adding pressure or releasing the key.
The actual dark slot is now visible beside the key, indicating a remaining offset. Lift clear and unwind before correcting the alignment.
Unwind the remaining yaw above the lock, using the clearly visible dark keyhole rather than its reflection to guide the next correction.
Correct the visible slot’s remaining yaw and small rightward image offset while holding insertion height constant.
Align the shaft tip with the actual round slot mouth, correct the small yaw overshoot, and test only a shallow descent.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for unexecuted motion. Lift clear and make a small pitch adjustment to inspect the shifted key.
Restore upright wrist alignment and raise clear of the lock. The key appears to have slid toward the wrist, so regain clearance before adjusting the pinch.
Briefly relax the left pinch slightly, well above the lock, to let the shifted key settle toward its bow; reclose and inspect rather than assuming retention.
Make one brief, slightly wider settling release above the lock, then reclose to recover a bow grip; retention remains uncertain.
The key visibly settled back toward the finger tips. Use one shorter settling pulse and reclose to improve the bow grip before insertion.
